Most burghers, craft masters and merchants read German in blackletter and Kurrent hand; Latin is the language of learning. Country people mostly cannot read.
- **Codex book and finding aids** [`codex_book`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/codex_book.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high Local: bookbinders and booksellers; Hofbibliothek; monastery libraries.
- **Woodblock printing** [`woodblock_printing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/woodblock_printing.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Used for calendars, playing cards, devotional prints and book ornaments.
- **Movable-type printing press** [`printing_press`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/printing_press.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. A few privileged presses work under censorship; Johann van Ghelen, university printer since 1678, has five. Most scholarly books come from Frankfurt, Nuremberg, Leipzig and the Netherlands. Local: Johann van Ghelen; the Cosmerovius printing house (court printers); Leopold Voigt (university printer). Elsewhere: Frankfurt and Leipzig book fairs; Amsterdam.
- **Reproducing images (woodcut, engraving, etching, lithography)** [`lithography_engraving`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lithography_engraving.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Copper engraving and etching serve maps, siege plans, portraits and theses. Mezzotint (1642) is known from prints. Lithography is unknown. Local: engravers working for the court and the printers; Daniel Suttinger's siege plans. Elsewhere: Augsburg and Nuremberg: the main print publishers.
- **Relay post and public mail** [`postal_system`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/postal_system.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The Counts Paar hold the hereditary court post (since 1624), with fixed post days and public rates; the Taxis run the Reich post. The siege cuts it off. Local: Hofpostamt of the Paar family; post routes to Linz, Prague, Graz, Pressburg, Venice.
- **Newspapers and periodicals** [`newspapers_periodicals`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/newspapers_periodicals.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. A censored weekly German Ordinari-Zeitung has appeared since the 1620s; van Ghelen holds the privilege (1678) for Latin and Italian papers. News is foreign and military, without comment. Local: Johann van Ghelen (Latin and Italian newspapers); Cosmerovius press (Ordinari Reichs-Zeitung). Elsewhere: Nuremberg, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Amsterdam: denser, freer newspapers; Wiennerisches Diarium only from 1703.
- **Scientific journal and peer review** [`scientific_journal`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_journal.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Journals arrive by post and through booksellers months late. No learned journal is edited in Vienna; physicians can publish in the Miscellanea curiosa. Elsewhere: London: Philosophical Transactions; Paris: Journal des sçavans; Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum (Otto Mencke, 1682).
- **Encyclopedias and dictionaries** [`encyclopedia_reference_works`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/encyclopedia_reference_works.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Latin compendia (Alsted 1630) and Moréri's French dictionary (1674) are in libraries. No German alphabetical encyclopedia exists. Local: Hofbibliothek; Jesuit college library.
- **Library catalogue and classification** [`library_catalogue`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/library_catalogue.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Lambeck (prefect 1663–1680) printed eight volumes of commentaries on the court library but no complete catalogue. Shelf lists by size and subject are usual. Local: Hofbibliothek. Elsewhere: Oxford: Bodleian printed catalogue (1674); Wolfenbüttel: ducal library.
- **Pencil, steel pen and durable ink** [`pencil_steel_pen`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pencil_steel_pen.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Writing is done with goose quill and iron-gall ink. Wood-cased graphite pencils come from Nuremberg and are used by engineers and artists. Metal pens are rare curiosities. Elsewhere: Nuremberg: pencil makers; Borrowdale, England: the graphite mine.
- **Shorthand (stenography)** [`shorthand`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/shorthand.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Scholars know of ancient Tironian notes. Chancery clerks use abbreviations only. No German system exists. Elsewhere: England: printed shorthand systems (Shelton, Rich) in common use.
- **Typewriter** [`typewriter`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/typewriter.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium
- **Copying documents (copying press, carbon paper, stencil duplicator)** [`copying_duplicating`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copying_duplicating.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept high. Every copy of a dispatch or order is written out by clerks. The chanceries would welcome anything faster. Local: Hofkanzlei, Hofkriegsrat and Hofkammer chanceries.
- **Braille (tactile writing for blind people)** [`braille_tactile_writing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/braille_tactile_writing.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Lana de Terzi's Prodromo (1670) sketches a touch-readable code for the blind; it stayed on paper. Blind people live by begging or music.
- **Sign languages of deaf people** [`sign_languages`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sign_languages.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Deaf people use home signs and are often held incapable in law. Bonet's Spanish manual alphabet (1620) is known to few. No teacher works in Vienna. Elsewhere: Spain: Bonet's method; England: Wallis and Holder teach deaf pupils.
- **Knowledge in the vernacular; translation movements** [`vernacular_translation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/vernacular_translation.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Sermons, ordinances, calendars and gunnery books are German; university teaching and science are Latin; the court speaks Italian and Spanish. Luther's Bible is forbidden. Local: Abraham a Sancta Clara (German preacher, in Graz in 1683).
- **Beacons, flag codes and heliograph** [`signal_beacons_flag_codes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/signal_beacons_flag_codes.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Chains of warning fires (Kreidfeuer) on hills and castles announce Turkish raids; bells sound the alarm. From 27 August rockets from St Stephen's tower signal to the relief army. Local: St Stephen's tower (observation post and rocket signals); Kreidfeuer stations in Lower Austria and Styria.
- **Optical telegraph (semaphore network)** [`optical_telegraph`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/optical_telegraph.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Signals carry one pre-agreed meaning. Spelling out messages with telescope and code is unknown; Hooke lectures on it in London in 1684. Local: spectacle and telescope makers; St Stephen's tower, Kahlenberg, Bisamberg in line of sight. Elsewhere: London: Robert Hooke (1684).
- **Standard time and time zones** [`standard_time_zones`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standard_time_zones.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Each town keeps its own time by sundial and tower clock. Nothing moves fast enough for the difference to matter.
